review_reference: Owner decisions in chat by D-Eminence, 2026-11-05 (about 12:00 UTC, relayed by the coordinator), for 0108 (records processing cover): D-a (lifetime) "staff whose direct-care access to the patient is active may do records processing (purpose healthcare-operations, read_records or write_records) for as long as that access lasts, not only for 24 hours from its start", superseding the 24-hour bound of decision 34(1) (0104 D7); D-b (shares) "an active 0095 patient share also covers it", any share level covering records-processing read and write as a PIN grant does under 0104 D7. D-b is a separately delimited alternative in the cover's body, so the owner may approve D-a alone (without D-b the sealed demo doctor, whose only grant is 0098's seeded share, still gets no cover). Numbered 0108, the next free number after production's 0107. Unsigned: reviewed_by is empty until the owner signs.
evidence: Single migration 0108_records_processing_cover_lifetime.sql, unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). WHAT IT DOES: CREATE OR REPLACE of identity.records_processing_direct_care_cover(uuid,text,uuid,uuid,text,timestamptz) (0104 D9) and its comment, nothing else. D-a: the 0104 bound at_time < starts_at + 24 hours is dropped and covered_until (and the ordering key) is the grant's expires_at instead of least(expires_at, starts_at + 24 hours); the cover still ends whenever the grant stops being active (revoked, PIN turned off, held by the cutover, membership or account ended). D-b: one more alternative next to 0104's approval and PIN ways (which are unchanged, now an EXISTS on identity.access_requests by the grant's request_id instead of an inner join): request_id null, no authorization method, granted_by_patient_id = patient_id, and a row in identity.patient_consent_shares with consent_grant_id = the grant, the same patient_id and membership_id; as for every covering grant: purpose direct-care, scope read_records or write_records, not break-glass, active, migration_hold_reason null, source_system 'hid'. Kept exactly from 0104 D6/D8: the same membership at the same facility on the live active account, ocr.job.write at each use, the patient 18 or over on the Africa/Lagos date with a date of birth, deny directives for records processing or direct care (0012's reading), break-glass/emergency and seeded or imported grants excluded, both purpose codes active (kill switch). Body md5 f3216bee48827dfba8073199b56ded67 (0104) before, 6928763d3b69f0e4b4acf96a6a255736 after. Signature, result TABLE(consent_grant_id uuid, covered_until timestamptz), owner, language sql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, cost, rows, parallel and ACL (hid_identity_runtime EXECUTE only, none for PUBLIC) unchanged, compared attribute by attribute after the replacement. identity.has_active_consent_grant untouched (md5 732d11892dd4e27e1ff9093ae3b7de5a before and after, attributes, owner and ACL compared). No table, column, constraint, policy, trigger, role, permission or grant change; runtime-grants.sql unchanged (its 0104 block names the same signature and applies cleanly twice); no row read or written. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's identity-api reads consent_grant_id and covered_until from the cover and answers expiresAt = covered_until (postgres-identity.provider.ts, unchanged but for a comment), so it reports the longer cover with no code change; OCR, EHR documents and every policy reach the cover through has_active_consent_grant by name. The website's patient wording ("for up to 24 hours") is the website lane's to update. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0001-0107 applied (ocr.claim_worker_job_fair md5 49b95651106e0aaa6f8bf6c8adcdb696 is the marker); not applied yet (the cover's body is not already 0108's, else '0108: already applied'); md5 of the cover (0104's), has_active_consent_grant (0104's), auth.membership_has_permission 65e3eaff93fe729fd5c5b986b80c9dd6 and identity.write_patient_share e7bce33a905c66e224f0fb7dff513701 (0095's, the share writer); the cover's attributes, arguments and result; the 55 columns read with their types and NOT NULLs (patient_consent_shares consent_grant_id, patient_id, membership_id uuid NOT NULL among them); one owner for identity.access_requests, identity.consent_grants, identity.patients, the cover and has_active_consent_grant, the applier it or a member with INHERIT and SET; that owner holds USAGE/CREATE on identity, USAGE on auth, SELECT on auth.accounts, the directive tables, the memberships, the purpose codes and identity.patient_consent_shares and EXECUTE on auth.membership_has_permission, never through a superuser's bypass; no forced row-level security on the tables the cover reads as its owner, and identity.patient_consent_shares (forced, 0095) has a permissive all-roles policy admitting the owner; the cover's ACL is 0104's. LOCKS (pg_locks before commit on a 0107 copy): ACCESS SHARE on identity.consent_grants, auth.accounts, identity.patients, identity.access_requests, identity.patient_consent_shares, identity.purpose_of_use_codes, identity.consent_directives, identity.consent_directive_versions and identity.staff_facility_memberships; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on the cover (its comment); catalog and the session's temporary objects; nothing on has_active_consent_grant. Apply time about 20 ms. Behind ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.patient_consent_shares the runner stopped after its 5 s lock_timeout with nothing applied; behind a writer of identity.consent_grants it applied at once. PROVED on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 clusters (created and deleted): FRESH install of all 109 files 0001-0108 with the migrations before the role bootstrap (0 runtime roles before; plan 109 pending, dry run rolled back, apply, 0 pending), role bootstrap and --verify-only pass, the file again answers '0108: already applied', runtime-grants.sql applied twice and the bootstrap run again pass, all 81 database suites pass (records-processing 140 cases). UPGRADE: a database built by base 605e971e's own runner, files and runtime-grants.sql (108 files, ledger last 0107, cover md5 f3216bee...; the updated suite fails there, 16 cases), plan 1 pending (0108 with this sha256), dry run rolled back (cover still 0104's), apply, 0 pending, the runner again applies nothing, the file again answers '0108: already applied'; cover owner, attributes and ACL identical before and after, and identical to the fresh install; 1221 non-owner grants before 0108, after it and after a bootstrap (as on the fresh install); runtime-grants.sql applied twice; all 81 suites pass. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passed with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds, baseline 108 files with the base's runtime-grants.sql, 109 integrated, declared exactly 0108; dry run rolled back, checksums kept, migration grants match runtime-grants.sql (2480), 188 row-security settings unchanged). Negative copies stop with nothing applied: a 0106 database ('0108: 0001-0107 must be applied first'), a share policy hiding rows from the owner (42501), a changed has_active_consent_grant body (md5 mismatch). Mutants of the cover body, each failing the suite: D-b removed (the D-a-only body the owner may choose: 11 share cases), the 24-hour bound restored (6 cases), source_system check removed (10s7), age check removed (5 cases), directive check removed (3 cases), D-b without the share row (10s21b); removing only the break-glass/scope/purpose checks is not observable (the consent_grants CHECK ties break_glass to the break_glass scope and a break-glass grant has an emergency request, so the other conditions already exclude it). SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/records-processing.integration.sql, 140 cases: 1g2 the new body's md5; 5b/6d a share now covers records processing; 10l-10o2 a three-day grant covered 24 hours and two days after its start, until a second before its end, not at its end, covered_until = expires_at; 10p-10q revoked not covered; 10s1-10s24 shares: named by the cover until its expires_at, replaced share no longer covers, view_only covers records-processing read and write while direct care reads only, a 7-day share covered two days on, a seeded (source_system not 'hid') share not covered, another membership or facility not covered, a deny directive for records processing at the share's facility, its withdrawal, revocation, under-18 and no date of birth not covered, a share row on break-glass not covered, a grant with no request and no share row not covered, the kill switch; order-routes-cannot-complete's d18 pin of the cover renewed to 0108's md5.
